h: Hillforts, Racetracks and the Test Valley
p: The trust's spot on the A303 at Weyhill puts it in the middle of chalk downland that's packed with history. Just to the south-west of Andover, Danebury is an Iron Age hillfort surrounded by huge earth ramparts, now a nature reserve with wildflowers, butterflies and big views. It's free to explore and great for kids who like running up and down banks pretending to defend a castle.

Next door to Weyhill, Thruxton Circuit is one of the fastest motor racing tracks in the country and hosts touring car and other race meetings through the year. On race days the roads get busy, so it's worth checking the calendar if you're planning a quiet visit.

For a farm day, Finkley Down Farm just outside Andover is a family favourite with farm animals, play barns and outdoor play. Stockbridge, a few miles south, is a pretty little town on the River Test, one of the world's most famous chalk streams, where trout can often be spotted from the bridges.
If you're heading west along the A303, Stonehenge is less than half an hour away, so combining it with a morning at the trust makes a cracking day of birds and ancient stones.
Practical tips: come with a few layers, as the meadows are open to the wind. Bring binoculars if you have them, as wild birds visit the site as well.
